questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I had originally wanted to go to a big city in the UK, but since no programmes were offered that fit my destinations and study path, I decided to do something different.
I wanted to go to an English-speaking country, but didn't feel that the US would suit me at the moment. Since Australia has always intrigued me, both culturally and nature-wise, I decided to go for it - the farthest possible destination from Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find the information. Emails, introduction information leaflets and the university-student pages provided information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I didn't get assistance since I didn't need it, but it was available for anyone who needed it. (transport from the airport, help with accommodation and so on).
I did get help with course planning during the introduction week when some of my classes clashed and other technical/IT help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It did take a lot of work and searching. I used
Flatmates.com.au
, but had to message a lot of people. I used the free version, so replies also took a considerable amount of time. I also didn't want to pay too much and still stay fairly close to campus/transport options
I know other people who stayed for multiple semesters found flats through friends closer to campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Living off campus is nice, but it can also be a bit limiting. Depending on where you live and who your friends are, most will likely live on or near campus, so it can be a bit challenging if you are the only one with considerable transportation time. It can also feel like you will miss out on some things if you need to leave early due to transport
It worked out great though, and I loved living off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Housing can be expensive. I know most people living on campus paid at least 7000kr. Living off campus was a bit cheaper for me, but I know that isn't always the case

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
When you make your application, you need to outline any courses with prerequisites that you plan on taking/might take. 
Then, as you get accepted and closer to the semester, you need to fill out course registration/study plan, which was also fairly easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could contact IT or a course admin/STOP 1 where they would be able to help with most things.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. Only one course was unsuccessful since it was the wrong semester (I don't know if they changed the semester it was running, or if I didn't check properly)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Have backup courses you want to take. Take a "fun" class that isn't necessarily relevant for your degree if you have enough elective points. UniMelb offer a lot of fun breadth courses (painting, education, music, wine courses and so on)
Make sure you don't mix up sem 1 and sem 2 courses as they are opposite to each other.
Also, make sure you check prerequisites and really look into whether you qualify.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took two first-year courses in physics and astronomy as part of my electives. Then I took a 2nd-year and a 3rd-year course in Geology. 
The geology courses were similar in difficulty level to those at UCPH. 
The physics course was difficult, but that could also be because it had been a very long time since I had done any physics. 
The astronomy class was also at a fairly okay level. The lectures clashed with my other classes though, so that made it a bit difficult to fully follow the course. (All lectures were filmed, so I could rewatch them)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar. Geology courses had the same style of lectures and practicals as I was used to from UCPH. As for the Physics and astronomy courses, I am guessing they have a similar style as UCPH as well. We had lectures and labs, as well as some calculation classes and TA hours.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ERTH20003 - Past Climates: Icehouse to Greenhouse
GEOL30007 - Geobiology
PHYC10003 - Physics 1
PHYC10008 - From the Solar System to the Cosmos

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked all the courses I took and would recommend them, but as I mentioned above, I would also recommend taking some courses that aren't necessarily related to your degree. UniMelb has a bunch of different courses that are good as electives and can give some "breathing room" in your week. Take a class just for fun

questions.answer: Not sure what was unexpected...

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Some groceries were cheaper while others were more expensive. Café drinks were less expensive and eating out was also a fair bit cheaper than in Copenhagen

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university has an incredible amount of clubs, sports and other activities. During the intro week there will be stands from almost all clubs and sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was a part of the hiking club, astronomy society, UMSU, and others. There are definitely going to be something for everyone

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Visit different suburbs of Melbourne. Try out some of the many markets they have, go to beaches. 
For weekend trips, I would recommend Philip Island, Mornington Peninsula, Wilson's prom, and Great Ocean Road. 
For mid-semester break I roadtripped Brisbane - Gold Coast - Sunshine Coast - Noosa. I also went to Sydney and loved it. After exams, I went on a long road trip to New Zealand with friends, and it was such a good trip. 
Some of the things I wish I had had time to do include is Tasmania, Great Barrier Reef, Ulluru, Perth, and Byron Bay.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. It is a big cultural city like many others, so it wasn't too hard

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be shy to initiate conversation in classes with someone you're sitting beside, or initiate a study session or coffee with a classmate you're working with. It is also good to go to different club events and similar, to meet local students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Not really any as far as I remember. 
It took some time to get used to the different driving lane and which side to look.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I liked a lot of it. There's a big social culture and coffee/tea culture, which is great. A lot of focus on being outside, being active and social.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it. Try and see as much as possible and try to take at least one class thats a "fun" class/not related to your degree/fairly easy.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not sure no...

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The whole overall experience, the memories, friends, and travel I got. It was incredible to try a univeristy in a different city and a different social culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trying to balance the academic side while also seeing and experiencing as much as possible (also with the budget I had available).

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
